fields.Front: List the four roles people take on when working with a DBMS.
fields.Back: Database Administrator (DBA); Database Designer; System Analyst / Application Programmer; End User.

fields.Front: Give at least two responsibilities of a Database Administrator (DBA).
fields.Back: Giving/revoking access; installing and upgrading the DBMS; monitoring usage; monitoring and improving performance; checking for security violations; backing up and restoring databases.

fields.Front: Give at least two responsibilities of a Database Designer.
fields.Back: Identifying all data to be stored; identifying relationships between data; creating a model of the data; structuring the data (picking tables); communicating with end users; creating views that satisfy end-user needs.

fields.Front: Give at least two responsibilities of a System Analyst / Application Programmer.
fields.Back: Determine end-user needs; develop specs; develop software that implements the specs in a language that talks to the database; test the implementation; communicate with end users.

fields.Front: Give two responsibilities of an End User.
fields.Back: Access the database by generating reports; access it via the application programmers' software to update, maintain and query it. Normally does not access the database directly (except a standalone user of a small personal database).

fields.Text: Backing up and restoring the database is the job of the {{c1::Database Administrator (DBA)}}; creating the data model is the job of the {{c2::Database Designer}}.
The role that normally does not access the database directly is the {{c1::end user}}.

fields.Front: How does the instructor summarize the DBA's position relative to database design?
fields.Back: The DBA is in charge of running the DBMS software, but is not the person who creates or designs databases.

fields.Text: DBA performance task the instructor mentions: fixing {{c1::queries that are running really slowly}}.
In this course you write code in {{c1::PHP}} that talks to a database that {{c2::already exists}} (MySQL or PostgreSQL).

fields.Front: Which of the four roles will you NOT take on in this course, and why?
fields.Back: DBA: the databases (PostgreSQL or MySQL) have already been installed by staff, so you will not install or administer a DBMS.

fields.Text: In this course you take on {{c1::three}} of the four roles: {{c2::database designer, application programmer and end user}}, but not {{c3::DBA}}.

fields.Front: Give the instructor's example of an end-user query, and say when you act as an end user in this course.
fields.Back: 'All the courses taught by Laura Reid.' You are an end user when testing your own software to make sure it does what you want.

fields.Front: Describe the database designer's job as the sequence the instructor gives.
fields.Back: Collect and identify all data to store; find the relationships between the data; create a model; use the model to create the database and decide the tables; verify every piece of data is stored and end users can run efficient queries.
